text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- 1996 consumer spending expected to be about 2.4 percent higher than in 1995.
-- Boeing has total of 645 orders for 1996 against Airbus's 300.
-- January 3 cabinet meeting to make to nominations to Bank of France monetary policy council.
-- Decree sets France Telecom's nominal share capital at 25 billion francs.
-- Utilities suppliers EDF and GDF to pay government 6.6 billion francs in dividends and settlement of payroll tax arrears.
-- Aerospatiale and Diehl team up to develop rocket launcher for US-European MLRS programme.
-- 1996 champagne sales reach record 250 million bottles.
-- Total joins Elf and Azerbaijan's Sicar on Caspian offshore oil production deal.
-- GAN will need seven to 10 billion franc cash injection from government before privatisation, but perhaps even more.
-- Auto insurance price war rolls over into 1997, with discounts of one to 10 percent threatening to erode margins.
-- Air transport accidents claim 1,900 lives in 1996.
-- French government certain to raise well over 600 billion francs on 1997 financial markets against 560 billion in 1996.
-- Credit Lyonnais to ask all 36,000 employees to accept job-saving 0.6 percent pay cut.
